clue.text: Makes furnace a must in a storm

indicators.note: a storm tosses things about, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A storm demands that a furnace be kept burning.
explanation.definitionFit: To manufacture is to produce goods, so the third-person verb is a direct synonym for makes.

clue.text: Former student in Minnesota getting into usual shenanigans

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it
shenanigans are mischief, so the word before them is jumbled

parts.note: MN is the postal abbreviation for Minnesota

explanation.surface: A graduate in Minnesota gets up to the usual pranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Minnesota' reads as a location, but 'in' is just a link and MN goes into the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a graduate of a school or college, someone who studied there in the past.

clue.text: University cops put away new model

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Campus police lock up a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' looks like jailing someone; it is the slang for eating.
explanation.definitionFit: An update is a revised version of a product, so it is a newer model of something.

clue.text: A block's photographer

parts.note: a dam is a block on a river, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Asking whose photographer a block has, in a terse question.
explanation.walkthrough: Ansel Adams was the American photographer famous for black-and-white pictures of Yosemite.
explanation.definitionFit: Ansel Adams is a celebrated landscape photographer, so his surname is an example of one.

clue.text: Where you can find Kosman and Picciotto at nine: hot, drunk

definitions.text: Where you can find Kosman and Picciotto

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: The setters can be found at nine o'clock, hot and drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The setters name themselves: their crossword runs in the magazine itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Kosman and Picciotto set this crossword for the magazine, so that publication is where readers find their puzzles.

clue.text: Determined, rose in rebellion over instrument

indicators.note: rebellion overturns order, so the flower's letters are rearranged

parts.note: a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Firmly, people rose up in revolt over a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a verb of revolt; it is the fodder. In a down clue 'over' places it above the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolute means firm in purpose and unwavering, a synonym of determined.

clue.text: Sleep quietly in ocean with vegetable

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the sleep and the quiet sign go within the ocean

parts.note: sea is a synonym for ocean
a nap is a short sleep
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone dozes peacefully at sea alongside a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' tells you the sleep and the quiet sign sit inside the ocean word, not after it; p for quietly is the musical marking piano.
explanation.definitionFit: The snap pea is a sweet edible-podded pea, eaten pod and all as a garden vegetable.

clue.text: During the morning, I finally shaved

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A morning routine: at some point I finally had a shave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' looks like it governs 'the morning', but it is the definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Amid means in the middle of or in the course of, so it can replace during as a preposition.

clue.text: Restless cop nuked a dessert

indicators.note: restless letters will not stay still, so they settle into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A jittery police officer blasts a dessert in the microwave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuked' sounds like the anagram signal, slang for microwaving, but the signal is 'Restless' and 'nuked' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pound cake is a dense butter cake served as a sweet course, an example of a dessert.

clue.text: Hidden danger of medication that absorbs ugly fat

indicators.note: something that absorbs takes another thing inside itself

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medication

indicators.note: ugly means misshapen, so the letters of the next word are deformed into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that a slimming drug that soaks up fat has a secret risk.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is an unexpected difficulty or trap, literally a concealed pit, so a hidden danger.

clue.text: Many bees could be shot, almost?

definitions.text: Many bees could be shot, almost?

parts.note: surface reading: a large crowd of insects that someone might try to shoot down
setter's reading: many Bs written out look like BBs, the small pellets fired from an air gun, so the crowd of bees is nearly a volley of shot

explanation.surface: A wonder whether a cloud of bees could be gunned down.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a pun: written as letters, bees are Bs, and BB is the pellet shot from an air rifle, hence 'almost'.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is the dense flying mass of honeybees leaving a hive with their queen, the usual collective for many bees.

clue.text: 10: a blockbuster, in principle

parts.note: the number written out as a word

explanation.surface: A note that the answer to 10 is a blockbuster, at least in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: '10:' looks like a cross-reference to 10 Across, but it is just the number ten; TENET is also the title of a blockbuster film.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine held to be true, the same idea as a principle.

clue.text: Raced around to shout, "A piece of onion is like a potato sometimes!"

indicators.note: the word for raced goes around, enclosing what follows it

explanation.surface: Someone races about yelling that an onion slice resembles a potato.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation reads as one exclamation, but only 'like a potato sometimes' is the definition; the rest builds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Scalloped potatoes are sliced and baked in a creamy sauce, one common way potatoes are served.

clue.text: Too invested in financial solutions

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so the answer sits within the following words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Too much money has gone into financial fixes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too' reads as an adverb of excess but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too are synonyms, both meaning in addition.

clue.text: Act of taking off damaged tapestries

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Removing tapestries from the wall after they have been spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' suggests removing the wall hangings; it means taking off clothes, and 'Act' is a stage act.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease is a performance in which someone removes clothing, a stage act of undressing.

clue.text: Running total including ruler's lecture

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the scrambled word wraps the ruler
running as in colours running: the letters bleed into a new order

explanation.surface: A cumulative tally that counts a monarch's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running total' is a stock phrase that hides the anagram signal. The 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a scolding or reprimand, and a lecture in this sense is a telling-off.

clue.text: Demystify reassembly of pin and axle

indicators.note: reassembly puts parts back together in a different arrangement

parts.note: the letters of pin and axle, the and being a joiner

explanation.surface: Instructions to make sense of putting a pin and axle back together.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to make it clear and understandable, removing its mystery.

clue.text: Those landing at the airport are largely dominating competitors

indicators.note: largely means mostly, so the word before loses its last letter

parts.note: are with its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: Planes coming in to land mostly outnumber rival carriers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'dominating' means sitting above, so the shortened word goes on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrivals are people or flights coming in, so passengers landing at an airport are its arrivals.

clue.text: Cryptic solver seen with Lois in a secluded location

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or disguised, so the letters that follow appear in disguise

parts.note: Lois Lane is Superman's companion, so Lane goes with Lois

explanation.surface: A crossword solver is spotted with someone called Lois somewhere private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic solver' looks like one phrase for a puzzler, but 'Cryptic' is the signal working on 'solver'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lovers' lane is a quiet out-of-the-way road where couples park, an idiom for a secluded spot.

clue.text: Change nearly brand-new critter

indicators.note: nearly means not quite, so the word for change stops a letter short

parts.note: vary, to change, missing its last letter

explanation.surface: Swapping an almost-new animal for another.
explanation.walkthrough: Varmint is an American folk word for a pest animal; critter is its folksy synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal American words for a creature, especially a troublesome wild animal.

clue.text: Cut cord at first, then jump

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: a hop is a small jump

explanation.surface: Instructions for a bungee jump: sever the cord first, then leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To chop is to cut with a sharp blow, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Banshee agitated former celebrity

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A wailing spirit gets upset about a faded star.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is someone whose fame or success is in the past, an idiom for a faded star.

clue.text: Representative image of Gardner with a sailor

parts.note: Ava Gardner was a Hollywood film star
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A portrait of the actress alongside a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gardner' could be any person; it is a cue for the actress's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is an icon or figure standing for a user online, an image that represents someone.

clue.text: Full of shame? Die from it in convulsions

indicators.note: convulsions are violent spasms, which throw the preceding letters into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone so ashamed they could die of it, writhing with embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is apt: mortified once meant put to death, echoing 'Die'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortified means deeply embarrassed or humiliated, a strong synonym for feeling ashamed.

clue.text: In the sound, Shamu valiantly provides transport

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, across the gap between them
the sound asks for what those letters say when spoken, not how they are spelt

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words, with mu said as moo

explanation.surface: Shamu the killer whale bravely gives rides in a coastal inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like the sea inlet where a whale swims; it is the spoken-aloud signal. Shamu is the SeaWorld orca. Mu, the Greek letter, is often said moo.
explanation.definitionFit: To move goods or people is to transport them from one place to another, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Launch floated down the river in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse means read from back to front

parts.note: to tube is to float down a river on an inner tube

explanation.surface: Someone floats downstream backwards for the start of a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A debut is a first appearance or opening, so it can stand for a launch as a noun.

clue.text: Credit card entails the termination of bright prospect

indicators.note: to entail is to involve or include, so the card's name holds the next letter

parts.note: Visa is a brand of credit card

indicators.note: the termination of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Taking out a credit card means the end of a rosy financial outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bright prospect' reads as one phrase for a hopeful future; only 'prospect' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a wide view of scenery, and prospect in this sense means an extensive outlook.

clue.text: There you have it! Virginia stores fossil fuel

indicators.note: a place that stores something keeps it inside, so the state's abbreviation holds the fuel

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: A triumphant announcement that Virginia has fossil fuel reserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Voilà is French borrowed into English as an exclamation presenting a result, meaning look, done.

clue.text: Intermediate wager we placed in Gone With the Wind

indicators.note: placed in means put inside, so the wager and the pronoun go inside the scrambled word
something gone with the wind is blown about, so the word before is scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone bets on the film Gone With the Wind.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title is split: its first word is the fodder and the rest signals the shuffle, so the title cannot be read as a unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between is an intermediary who carries messages between two parties, here used as an intermediate.

clue.text: Tenors' parts required to show element of manliness

parts.note: surface reading: the vocal lines written for tenors in a choir or opera
setter's reading: a tenor's male parts, the testes, are needed to produce the hormone behind masculine traits

explanation.surface: A choirmaster says tenor lines must be sung with some machismo.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is on 'parts': not sung music but the male anatomy that makes the hormone. 'Element' is loose, since the answer is a hormone, not an element.
explanation.definitionFit: This steroid hormone drives male traits such as a deep voice and facial hair, so it underlies manliness.
